# Introduction

This report contains the per-sample analyses performed during the pipeline
execution, which include quality controls, filtering, dimensionality reduction,
clustering, differential expression and spatial analyses. If you ran the
pipeline without the `--skip_integration` parameter (which is the default), you
can find the report for the integrated data in the `integration/reports/`
directory.

In several cases throughout the report, figures are shown in _tabsets_, where
you can click on different tabs to show _e.g._ different quality metrics or
genes. You can also click each individual figure to see it in full screen.

```{python parameters}
#| tags: [parameters]
input_sdata = "sdata.zarr"
n_top_svgs = 20
n_top_markers = 250
artifact_dir = "artifacts"
```

```{python common-functions}
def create_tabset(content):
    """
    Programmatically create tabsets with headers and plots.

    Arguments:
        content (list): A list of (str, Figure) tuples
    """
    display(Markdown('::: {.panel-tabset}'))
    for name, fig in content:
        display(Markdown(f"#### {name}"))
        display(fig)
        plt.close()
        display(Markdown(f" "))
    display(Markdown(':::'))

def save_figure(fig, filename, dpi=150):
    """
    Save figure to artefact directory.

    Arguments:
        fig (Figure): The figure object to be saved
        filename (str): The file name to be used
        dpi (int): The DPI to use
    """
    fig.savefig(
        os.path.join(artifact_dir, filename),
        dpi=dpi,
        bbox_inches='tight'
    )

def display_table(table, hide_index=True, format_dict=None):
    """
    Display a data frame as a table with default styling with optional removal
    of the axis and the functionality to supply formatting dictionary.

    Arguments:
        table (DataFrame): The data frame to be displayed
        hide_index (boolean): Whether to hide the data frame index or not
        format_dict (dict): A dictionary with column-specific formatting
    """

    # Default style with nf-core green hover and right alignment for all columns
    # except the first one
    styles = [
        {'selector': 'tbody tr:hover', 'props': [('background-color', '#D5F6E4')]},
        {'selector': 'td, th', 'props': [
            ('text-align', 'right')
        ]},
        {'selector': 'td:first-child, th:first-child', 'props': [
            ('text-align', 'left')
        ]}
    ]
    styled = table.style.set_table_styles(styles)

    if hide_index:
        styled = styled.hide(axis='index')

    if format_dict:
        styled = styled.format(format_dict)

    display(styled)
```

# Quality controls

## QC metrics distribution

The following plots show the distribution of quality control metrics across all
spots.

```{python qc-metrics}
#| output: false
# Check which QC columns are available
qc_metrics_map = [
    ('total_counts', 'Total counts'),
    ('n_genes_by_counts', 'Genes per spot'),
    ('pct_counts_mt', 'Mito %'),
    ('pct_counts_ribo', 'Ribo %'),
    ('pct_counts_hb', 'Hb %'),
]
qc_metrics = [(col, label) for col, label in qc_metrics_map if col in adata.obs]

# Loop over metrics and store plots in list
qc_metrics_plots = []
has_qc = len(qc_metrics) > 0
if has_qc:
    for col, label in qc_metrics:
        fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(7, 5), constrained_layout=True)
        ax.hist(adata.obs[col].values, bins=50, edgecolor='black', alpha=0.7)
        ax.set_xlabel(label)
        ax.set_ylabel('Frequency')
        ax.axvline(adata.obs[col].median(), color='red', linestyle='--',
            label=f'Median: {adata.obs[col].median():.1f}')
        ax.legend(fontsize=8)
        save_figure(fig, f'qc-distribution-{col}.png')
        qc_metrics_plots.append((label, fig))
else:
    print("No QC metrics found in the data.")
```

# Highly variable genes

The following plot shows the dispersion and mean expression of all genes present
in the dataset, as well as which of the genes are considered highly variable.

```{python hvgs}
if 'highly_variable' in adata.var.columns:
    n_hvg = adata.var['highly_variable'].sum()
    display(Markdown(f"Number of highly variable genes: `{n_hvg}`"))

    if 'means' in adata.var.columns and 'dispersions_norm' in adata.var.columns:
        fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(7, 5), constrained_layout=True)

        hvg_mask = adata.var['highly_variable']

        ax.scatter(
            adata.var.loc[~hvg_mask, 'means'],
            adata.var.loc[~hvg_mask, 'dispersions_norm'],
            s=3, alpha=0.3, c='grey', label='Other genes'
        )
        ax.scatter(
            adata.var.loc[hvg_mask, 'means'],
            adata.var.loc[hvg_mask, 'dispersions_norm'],
            s=3, alpha=0.5, c='red', label='Highly variable'
        )

        ax.set_xlabel('Mean expression')
        ax.set_ylabel('Normalized dispersion')
        ax.set_title('Highly Variable Genes')
        ax.legend()
        save_figure(fig, 'highly-variable-genes.png')
        plt.show()
else:
    print("Highly variable gene information not found.")
```

# Dimensionality reduction

## PCA

The following plots show the results of the _Principal Component Analysis_ (PCA)
and its first two principal components, as well as the variance explained for
all of the components.

```{python pca}
if 'X_pca' in adata.obsm:
    fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(7, 3.5), constrained_layout=True)

    # PCA scatter plot coloured by clusters if available
    if 'clusters' in adata.obs:
        sc.pl.pca(adata, color='clusters', ax=axes[0], show=False,
            title='PCA')
    else:
        sc.pl.pca(adata, ax=axes[0], show=False, title='PCA')

    # Variance explained
    if 'pca' in adata.uns and 'variance_ratio' in adata.uns['pca']:
        variance_ratio = adata.uns['pca']['variance_ratio']
        cumulative_var = np.cumsum(variance_ratio)
        n_pcs = len(variance_ratio)

        axes[1].bar(range(1, n_pcs + 1), variance_ratio, alpha=0.7,
            label='Individual')
        axes[1].plot(range(1, n_pcs + 1), cumulative_var, 'r-', marker='o',
            markersize=3, label='Cumulative')
        axes[1].set_xlabel('Principal Component')
        axes[1].set_ylabel('Variance Explained')
        axes[1].set_title('PCA Variance Explained')
        axes[1].legend()
        axes[1].set_xlim(0, min(n_pcs + 1, 51))
    save_figure(fig, 'pca.png')
    plt.show()

    if 'pca' in adata.uns and 'variance_ratio' in adata.uns['pca']:
        display(Markdown(f"Variance explained by PC1: `{variance_ratio[0]:.2%}`"))
        display(Markdown(f"Variance explained by PC1-10: `{cumulative_var[9]:.2%}`"))
        if len(cumulative_var) >= 20:
            display(Markdown(f"Variance explained by PC1-20: `{cumulative_var[19]:.2%}`"))
else:
    print("PCA results not found.")
```

## Cluster statistics

The following table shows a summary of each cluster in the dataset, including
the number of spots, the proportion of spots in each cluster compared to the
dataset as a whole, as well as the mean counts and the mean number of genes for
each cluster.

```{python}
if 'clusters' in adata.obs:
    agg_dict = {'clusters': ('clusters', 'size')}

    if 'total_counts' in adata.obs:
        agg_dict['Mean counts'] = ('total_counts', 'mean')
    if 'n_genes_by_counts' in adata.obs:
        agg_dict['Mean genes'] = ('n_genes_by_counts', 'mean')

    cluster_stats = adata.obs.groupby('clusters').agg(**agg_dict)
    cluster_stats.columns = ['Spots', 'Mean counts', 'Mean genes']
    cluster_stats['Percentage'] = (cluster_stats['Spots'] / len(adata) * 100)

    # Reorder columns
    column_order = ['Spots', 'Percentage', 'Mean counts', 'Mean genes']
    cluster_stats = cluster_stats[column_order]

    # Create `Cluster` column from index
    cluster_stats = cluster_stats.sort_index().reset_index()
    cluster_stats.columns = ['Cluster'] + column_order

    # Apply table styling and display
    format_dict = {
        'Percentage': '{:.1f} %',
        'Mean counts': '{:.1f}',
        'Mean genes': '{:.1f}'
    }
    display_table(cluster_stats, format_dict=format_dict)
```

## Tables of differential genes per cluster

```{python degs-search-script}
# add table search function
# One handler serves every table in the document; the ids of the box and of the table it
# filters are passed in, which is what keeps a search local to its own table.

html = """
<script>
function searchTable(inputId, containerId) {
    let input = document.getElementById(inputId).value.toLowerCase();
    let rows = document.querySelectorAll('#' + containerId + ' tbody tr');
    rows.forEach(row => {
        let rowText = row.textContent.toLowerCase();

        if (rowText.includes(input)) {
            row.style.display = '';
        } else {
            row.style.display = 'none';
        }
    });
}

function sortTable(containerId, colIndex) {
    let table = document.querySelector('#' + containerId + ' table');
    let tbody = table.tBodies[0];
    let rows = Array.from(tbody.rows);

    // Clicking the column that is already sorted reverses it, any other column starts ascending.
    let sorted = table.getAttribute('data-sort-col');
    let ascending = !(sorted === String(colIndex) && table.getAttribute('data-sort-dir') === 'asc');

    let cell = row => row.cells[colIndex].textContent.trim();
    let numeric = rows.every(row => cell(row) === '' || !isNaN(parseFloat(cell(row))));

    rows.sort((a, b) => {
        let x = cell(a);
        let y = cell(b);
        let order = numeric ? parseFloat(x) - parseFloat(y) : x.localeCompare(y);
        return ascending ? order : -order;
    });

    rows.forEach(row => tbody.appendChild(row));
    table.setAttribute('data-sort-col', colIndex);
    table.setAttribute('data-sort-dir', ascending ? 'asc' : 'desc');
}
</script>
"""
if has_markers:
    display(HTML(html))
```

```{python degs-search-helpers}
# helper functions for creating HTML table

def sortable_headers(table_html: str, table_name: str) -> str:
    """
    Turn the header cells of a rendered table into sort handles.

    Every `<th>` of the header row gets an onclick calling `sortTable` with its own column
    index, so a reader can order the genes by fold change, p-value or any other column. The
    handler decides numeric or text ordering from the values themselves, which is why the
    column type does not have to be passed on here.
    """
    header = re.search(r'<thead>.*?</thead>', table_html, flags=re.DOTALL)
    if header is None:
        return table_html

    index = itertools.count()

    def handle(match):
        return (
            "<th style='cursor: pointer' title='Click to sort' onclick=\"sortTable('"
            + table_name + "', " + str(next(index)) + ")\">" + match.group(1) + " &#8645;</th>"
        )

    return table_html.replace(
        header.group(0), re.sub(r'<th>(.*?)</th>', handle, header.group(0), flags=re.DOTALL)
    )


def create_search_table_html(df: pd.DataFrame, search_text: str,
                             sbox_name: str, table_name: str, ntop: int=100,
                             lookupFunction: str="searchTable") -> str:
    """
    Creates HTML string for searchable table

    Parameters
    ----------
    df: pd.DataFrame
        Pandas DataFrame to be turned into searchable table
    search_text: str
        Text that will be displayed in search box before typing
    sbox_name: str
        Unique searchbox ID that will be assigned
    table_name: str
        Unique table ID that will be assigned
    ntop: int
        Limit the number of rows to this number to avoid giant HTMLs
    lookupFunction: str
        JavaScript function for text search, has to be defined beforehand.

    Returns
    -------
    str
        HTML table string that can be displayed with IPython.display.HTML
    """

    # input search box
    table_html = "<input type='text' id='" + sbox_name + "' onkeyup=\"" + lookupFunction + "('" + sbox_name + "', '" + table_name + "')\" "
    table_html += "placeholder='" + search_text + "'"
    table_html += "style='width: 100%; max-width: 300px; padding: 10px; margin-top: 12px; font-family: sans-serif; border: 1px solid #D1D5DB; border-radius: 4px;'>"

    # table, with every header cell wired to the sort handler of its own column
    table_body = sortable_headers(df.head(ntop).to_html(index=False), table_name)
    table_html += "<div id=" + table_name + " style='overflow-y: scroll; max-height: 400px'>" + table_body + "</div>"

    return table_html
```

# Spatially variable genes

## Spatial autocorrelation

```{python spatial-autocorrelation}
# Check for spatial autocorrelation results
svg_key = None
svg_method = None
svg_stat = None
if 'moranI' in adata.uns:
    svg_key = 'moranI'
    svg_method = "Moran's I"
    svg_stat = 'I'
elif 'gearyC' in adata.uns:
    svg_key = 'gearyC'
    svg_method = "Geary's C"
    svg_stat = 'C'

if svg_key:
    svg_df = adata.uns[svg_key]
    n_svg = len(svg_df)
    display(Markdown(f"Spatial autocorrelation method: `{svg_method}`"))
    display(Markdown(f"Number of genes analyzed: `{n_svg}`"))

    # Save top SVGs to CSV
    svg_df.head(100).to_csv(os.path.join(artifact_dir, 'top_spatially_variable_genes.csv'))
```

## Top spatially variable genes

The following table shows the top spatially variable genes, along with their
respective spatial autocorrelation statistic (Moran's I or Geary's C) and
adjusted p-value.

```{python}
if svg_key:
    n_display = n_top_svgs
    top_svg = svg_df.head(n_display).copy()
    top_svg['Gene'] = top_svg.index
    top_svg['Rank'] = range(1, len(top_svg) + 1)
    top_svg = top_svg[['Rank', 'Gene', svg_stat, 'pval_norm_fdr_bh']]
    top_svg.columns = ['Rank', 'Gene', svg_method, 'Adj. p-value']
    format_dict = {
        svg_method: '{:.3f}',
        'Adj. p-value': '{:.3g}'
    }
    display_table(top_svg, format_dict=format_dict)
```

## Spatial expression of top SVGs

The following figures show the spatial expression of the top 15 spatially
variable genes.

```{python svg-plots}
#| output: false
has_spatial_svg = svg_key and has_spatial
if has_spatial_svg:
    top_genes = svg_df.head(9).index.tolist()

    # Filter to genes that exist in the data
    top_genes = [gene for gene in top_genes if gene in adata.var_names]

    svg_plots = []
    for gene in top_genes:
        fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(7, 5), constrained_layout=True)
        sc.pl.spatial(
            adata,
            color=gene,
            ax=ax,
            show=False,
            title=gene,
            frameon=False,
            library_id=f"{sample_id}_hires_image"
        )
        svg_plots.append((gene, fig))
        save_figure(fig, f'spatial-{gene}.png')
    else:
        print("No valid genes found for spatial plotting.")
```

# Summary

```{python}
summary_sections = []

# Data overview
summary_sections.append(
    f"#### Data overview\n"
    f"- **Sample**: `{sample_id}`\n"
    f"- **Spots**: `{n_spots}`\n"
    f"- **Genes**: `{n_genes}`\n"
)

# QC summary
if 'total_counts' in adata.obs:
    median_counts = adata.obs['total_counts'].median()
    median_genes = adata.obs['n_genes_by_counts'].median() if \
        'n_genes_by_counts' in adata.obs else 'N/A'
    summary_sections.append(
        f"#### Quality controls\n"
        f"- **Median counts per spot**: `{median_counts:,.0f}`\n"
        f"- **Median genes per spot**: `{median_genes:,.0f}`\n"
    )

# Clustering summary
if 'clusters' in adata.obs:
    n_clusters = adata.obs['clusters'].nunique()
    summary_sections.append(
        f"#### Clustering\n"
        f"- **Number of clusters**: `{n_clusters}`\n"
        f"- **Algorithm**: `Leiden`\n"
    )

# SVG summary
if svg_key:
    n_sig = (svg_df['pval_norm_fdr_bh'] < 0.05).sum() if \
        'pval_norm_fdr_bh' in svg_df.columns else 'N/A'
    top_gene = svg_df.index[0]
    summary_sections.append(
        f"#### Spatially variable genes\n"
        f"- **Method**: `{svg_method}`\n"
        f"- **Significant genes (FDR < 0.05)**: `{n_sig}`\n"
        f"- **Top gene**: `{top_gene}`"
    )

display(Markdown("\n".join(summary_sections)))
```

# Build list of package versions
packages = ['scanpy', 'squidpy', 'spatialdata', 'anndata', 'numpy', 'pandas',

    try:
        versions[pkg] = importlib.metadata.version(pkg)

# Build and write session info table
session_info = pd.DataFrame(
    [('python', platform.python_version())] + list(versions.items()),

)
